messages:
jorge: Heads-up: halley13b (13B) int4 canary moved into soak last night. We're seeing sporadic CUDA OOMs during overlapping long generations (max_new_tokens=600). Posting summary + hypotheses.

sasha: thanks. environment? hosted dedicated pool? any recent runtime changes?

jorge: hosted, small dedicated pool (2 cards). No kernel changes overnight. OOM excerpt: ```
2026-02-19T02:41:03Z E runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (requested 1.1GiB)
serve/runtime/kv_cache.go:158 allocateLocal
serve/runtime/allocator.go:76 allocateChunk
```
Happens typically when 4+ concurrent requests spawn long decodes.

maya: did you try lowering defaults? also curious if int4 wiring increases fragmentation.

jorge: quick A/B: int8 baseline with max_new_tokens=600 -> no OOMs at 50qps bursts, p99 ~420ms. int4 with same defaults -> OOM rate ~0.035% over 50k reqs, p99 ~290ms. So int4 faster but fragile under heavy parallel long-gen.

liam: two-pronged fix: reduce default_max_new_tokens for hosted default to 200 for halley13b-int4, and change batching policy: max_batch_size=5, batch_window_ms=10. Also enable slot compactor at 45s and reduce slot reservation for prefetched KV. That should cut peak resident set.

maya: can we add an adaptive path: request with requested max_new_tokens>350 should go to int8 by routing rule for safety? keeps UX for short gens but avoids tail OOMs.

sasha: love that. we'll add a routing policy that checks (model_variant==int4 && requested_max_new_tokens>350) -> route to halley13b-int8. Also add runtime overcommit guard: if free_gpu_mem < 1.5GiB, fail fast with 429 and hint to client.

eng-ml-bot: Canary update queued: halley13b-int4 config patch by jorge. Rollout plan: 5% -> 30% in 20m if no errors.

jorge: ran a soak with new config (default_max_new_tokens=200, batch_size=5, compactor=45s) for 24h: results below.

maya: paste numbers?

jorge: short table (20k sample windows):
- int8 baseline (old config): p50 36ms, p95 110ms, p99 420ms, OOMs 0
- int4 old config: p50 28ms, p95 90ms, p99 290ms, OOMs 7
- int4 new config: p50 30ms, p95 95ms, p99 310ms, OOMs 0
quality checkpoints (sacreBLEU on long-summary set): int8 34.2, int4 old 33.0, int4 new 33.1

liam: so new config removes OOMs and restores most of the int4 perf; sacreBLEU still ~1.1 down vs int8. acceptable if documented.

maya: also ran a kernel-level mem fragmentation trace: seeing many small free blocks after large allocations - compactor reduced block count by ~48% over 1h.

sasha: great. two follow-ups: (1) add canary gating eval that includes 5 prompts >400 tokens, fail promotion if sacreBLEU drop >1.5% or OOM rate >0.05% (2) update model catalog blurb to document "int4: cost-first, expect ~1% quality drop on long-context summarization; prefer int8 for >350 token gens or Dedicated \"quality-first\" customers."

liam: for Dedicated we should expose a cluster-level default_max_new_tokens override and a quant-preference flag. ops already asked for that.

jorge: action items: 
- jorge: ship canary config (done) and monitor next 6h
- maya: upload full CSVs + fragmentation trace to model-onboard doc and add a short readme on our heuristics
- liam: implement routing rule for requested_max_new_tokens>350 -> int8 fallback and add alert if OOM rate >0.02%
- sasha: draft catalog note and add dedicated toggle doc

eng-ml-bot: Canary promoted to 30% traffic after 20m: no fatal errors detected.

maya: sanity check on production-like 80qps burst with mixed short/long gens: int4 new config had 0 OOMs across 40k requests, p99 ~315ms, sacreBLEU stable at 33.1.

sasha: sounds like safe to promote further tomorrow if soak remains clean. Thanks all. :party-parrot:

liam: let's ensure the rollout policy includes automatic fallback to int8 if any OOMs or sacreBLEU regression beyond threshold. we can reuse the rollout-fallback module.

jorge: noted. closing this triage thread; follow-ups in #model-onboard-1745.

maya: thanks everyone. good example of balancing perf vs reliability. :ok_hand:
